messages:
sam: heads up — saw a crash in prod when a customer pushed a feature flag with an unexpected object shape. stack trace points to config deserialization in the routing layer.
leah: ugh, that was from the merchant where we let arbitrary JSON through in flags, right? any quick mitigation?
dmitri: rolled a hotfix to defensive-parse that catches unknown fields and rejects them with a 400. ops-bot: incident #INC-2026-442 created for config-deser-errors.
sam: thanks. short-term patch is fine but we need a long-term plan — proposal: introduce typed config contracts for runtime flags (optional opt-in to start) + console validation so customers get immediate lint errors before apply.
maya: +1. DevEx can surface schema diffs in the console and provide a preview of failing canaries. Could show a small example payload and which services would reject it.
leah: also need migration story. When contracts tighten, existing flag values might not conform. we should support: 1) conservative enforcement mode (dry-run + telemetry) 2) hard-enforce after 30 days 3) automated migrate suggestions where possible.
dmitri: runtime fallback is crucial. Suggest adding a compatibility layer: if a flag fails strict validation, route to a safe-default variant and emit a warning metric. That avoids customer-visible crashes.
anya: +ops. For telemetry gating, we can create a new sampling tag on config-change events: "contract_dryrun_fail". console shows % of requests that would be affected.
sam: good. Implementation sketch: - add optional JSON Schema field on config definitions - store versioned schema with each config commit - console runs schema validation for preview and shows examples - server uses schema vX to validate on apply; if in dry-run, record violations but still accept; if enforced, reject.
maya: UX note — when users upload a schema, show a preview of impacted services and an estimated rollout risk score (based on number of tenants, recent update cadence, and historical config flakiness).
leah: need API contract for infra teams: new endpoints: POST /configs/:id/schemas, GET /configs/:id/schema-history, POST /configs/:id/validate (payload). Also add header X-Config-Dryrun: true for server-side validation runs.
dmitri: agree — also add a server-side flag to treat schema changes as non-breaking by default. We should require an explicit "enforce":true to flip enforcement. Mirror our feature-flag rollout safety model.
ops-bot: deploy-check: unit tests for schema validation present? -> failed on dmitri/defensive-parse branch.
anya: i'll wire telemetry: two new counters: config.schema.validate.dryrun.fail and config.schema.apply.rejected. Plus a gRPC audit event for each schema change.
sam: compatibility concerns: some services accept dynamic typed fields (e.g., plugin metadata). proposal: allow schema to include "openProperties": true to allow future fields. default is closed.
maya: console should show a human readable diff and sample API requests that would fail. we can reuse the existing preview engine but need a new renderer for schema errors.
leah: rollout plan: week 0-1: internal alpha (platform only) with dry-run only and telemetry; week 2-3: beta with customer opt-in in console; week 4+: default dry-run for all; week 8: enforcement toggle available for orgs that pass validation thresholds; week 12: auto-enforce for new configs (historical exempt).
dmitri: operations checklist: upgrade runtime libs to new serde version, add schema cache invalidation hook, instrument per-node fallback counters, and add a graceful degrade route for requests that hit missing schema.
anya: telemetry thresholds for enforcement: require less than 0.1% dry-run failure rate across 7 days and less than 3 customers with >1% failures. metrics should be visible in console rollout page.
maya: canary UX: allow customers to opt into staged enforcement by percentage and by tenant list. console shows projected affected traffic.
sam: outstanding questions: - storage format for schemas (proto vs json-schema)? json-schema seems flexible and already supported by many libs. - do we allow multiple schema types per config? (eg: yaml-blobs)
dmitri: prefer JSON Schema v2020. It's widely adopted and has validators in all languages. storing as JSON is straightforward. we can add a small adapter layer for anything else.
leah: security: adding schema upload needs ACL checks and malware scanning on content. also rate-limit schema registers to avoid noisy revalidation storms.
anya: i'll add an alert if schema upload rate > 10/min/org.
maya: doc checklist for DevEx: console help flow, sample migration scripts, SDK helper to run local validation (npm and py packages), and a migration playground with fake tenants.
sam: ok i'll create an RFC PR today with the sketch and timeline. thanks everyone — big step but should stop more runtime panics.
ops-bot: incident #INC-2026-442 resolved: hotfix deployed, defensive-parse enabled across fleet.
leah: follow-up: can we add a small runnable example in the RFC showing an incompatible change and the console error? that'll make the story tangible.
sam: will add — ping me in thread if you want to pair on the sample schemas.
dmitri: i'll start a branch for the serde upgrade and wire the schema cache.
anya: telemetry PR incoming after branch.
maya: I'll mock the console screens and put them in figma. :thumbsup:
sam: moving to action items: sam -> RFC, dmitri -> serde branch, maya -> console mocks, anya -> telemetry, leah -> API endpoints + ACLs. timeline per rollout plan above.
leah: thanks team.
